text: You pull into a busy area, needing a parking spot. All you want is a single, open space. Ready to pay, ready to park, just point the way!
You enter the parking maze, turning down aisle after aisle with hopeful anticipation. Surely, one of these spots must be open. You follow the arrows, searching.
But every sign flashes 'FULL', or every space is taken. Your hope turns to frustration as you loop around, seeing an endless sea of parked cars.
The invisible system is simple: supply and demand. Not enough spots for everyone. And even if one opens, *finding* it takes precious time.
This 'search friction' means you spend minutes, endlessly circling. The system forces you to waste your time and gas, all to locate something that likely isn't there.
Now you see: it's not bad luck, it's the design. Tomorrow, you'll still need a spot, but you'll understand why the search feels impossible.
